VII. IRREVERSIBLE AND IRRETRIEVABLE COMMITMENT RESOURCES
Land acquired under authority of the proposed legislation will be committed to use for endangered species habitat. Each day of commitment is irretrievable, and production of a day of use for some other purpose is lost. Nevertheless, this commitment is not perpetual because the use of the land acquired could be changed by Congressional action at any time.
Federal authority provided by the proposed legislation or State programs encouraged by it will stop the killing of any species threatened with extinction and commercial traffic in its parts or products. The same constraints on use can be applied at the discretion of the Secretary on those species likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction. But this commitment is not irreversible or irretrievable because the Secretary may ultimately remove any species from the list thereby freeing them from Federal protection. Consumptive uses could then be restored.
If the proposed legislation is not enacted, chances are much greater that species and subspecies will become extinct and that more species and subspecies will become endangered and extirpated. The action itself provides for no irreversible trends that cannot be stopped or turned around by changes in legislative policy. The only irretrievable commitment of resources would be economic loses sustained by some people who trade in animals and their products and changes in annual production of alternative resources from lands acquired for endangered species habitat.
Without the proposed legislation, or with modification of some of its provisions, more species and subspecies and some populations will become extinct. This would be an irretrievable loss.
